reviews.title: Great product, but price jumped to an unreasonable price in less than 3 years
reviews.comment:
I got me a pair of these chips in 2023 at $224 here on Amazon. 64GB (2x32GB). Installed them on my Asus ROG Strix Z-690E motherboard with an i9-13900k and RTX 4090. Went into the BIOS and enabled the XMP profile at the full 6400MHz speed. Works perfectly! No slowdown, no crashes, no overheating!
I have been using this RAM since 2023 and have had no problems at all. I use it on AAA latest games including Cyberpunk, RDR2, Helldivers 2, Doom 2016, Doom Eternal, Doom the Dark Ages, Spiderman Remastered, Spiderman: Miles, GTA V remastered and many others all at 4k, 240hz, max settings, raytracing (overdrive or fastest performance depending on game), and no problems, no crashes, no hangs, and some game sessions longer than a few hours. Also play some VR games and lots of older classic retro games as well. No problems at all.
I also play a lot of Starcraft2 at the max settings. This game doesn't use a lot of RAM per-se, but in an epic 4v4 online battle and all 8 players building and attacking with 200PSI each, it will bring most gaming PCs to their knees. This one keeps the framerate above 100FPS which is insane. Also at the start of online games you will hit the game max framerate of 512FPS on most maps which is also insane to me since I have never seen any gaming PC ever hit 512 FPS before! I know its not just the RAM and probably a combination of the GPU/CPU as well, but with this RAM it has been a smooth ride and incredibly great speed in such an intense game.
Beyond gaming I am also a Graphic Designer, Animator and 3D modeler. With Photoshop, Illustrator, Flash, Dreamweaver and InDesign everything has been buttery smooth, super fast and zero problems. With After Effects and DaVinci Resolve, same deal. I am able to easily scrub 4K project files with no slowdown, no pauses and no crashes.  With Blender 3D I recently created the largest and most detailed project I have ever built. I created a realistic country club for a recent client. Thousands of subtle details, tons of polygons, gigabytes of textures, lots of effects including emission, reflections, HDRI sky and post rendering glows. I am still able to move around the 3D scene, create & edit models and render shots flawlessly and super smooth!
My one and only problem with this RAM is that I want to buy more of it, but I just saw that the price is now $999 as of 4/7/2026. This is the most disgusting inflation I have ever seen in my life. This is RAM, not a CPU, not GPU, not a cellphone and not a car or a truck. The price should be $224, not $1000. That is slightly less than 500% inflation!
I would suggest to everyone to not buy this RAM until they bring the price back down to the $200 price range. This is just disgusting and beyond words. If the price rose by a reasonable inflation rate of 3%, then it would be $230 today and not one penny shy of one thousand dollars!
And yes, I know it is industry-wide and not just Corsair and not just this specific model of RAM. The entire industry needs to fix this problem.
reviews.author: J. Brack

reviews.title: Beautiful, powerful, and smart RGB RAM almost perfect!
reviews.comment:
I’m really impressed with these Corsair 32GB CL32 RAM sticks. It feels like they were made just for me! The RGB looks amazing and can be easily controlled with iCUE software  very stylish and intelligent design. I bought them during a discount, so it was a great deal.
On my ASUS TUF Gaming Z790 motherboard, the RAM runs at 6400 MHz with XMP enabled, but after around 15–20 minutes of gaming (Far Cry 6 or Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War 2019), the system freezes and crashes. When I set the RAM to the standard 4800 MHz (XMP disabled), everything works perfectly. I haven’t fully investigated the cause yet, but aside from that, these RAMs are absolutely fantastic.
Thank you Corsair and Amazon!

reviews.title: Simple install, one click guaranteed 6400 mhz overclock speed
reviews.comment:
What I like most about Corsair hardware (as opposed to their software which is sadly lacking, e.g. iCue suite of control software, is that it just works well and right out of the box.
Bought high speed ram from Corsair before so was not disappointed when as expected it just worked with one click in my bios settings. Installed the 64 GB ram kit, turned on PC which went into BIOS as expected, RAM recognized, click to enable XMP for pre-configured profile #1 and done.
Stable, easy, guaranteed 6400 overclock speed. Corsair is never the cheapest, not really highest either, and it's worth ease of mind to pay the 'brand price' markup. I've no idea when these RGB lights will wear out, but my last kit is going strong 4 years of almost non-stop usage (awake or in sleep mode where the color is still lit).
I suspect it's a moot point, because the RAM / PC will be so vastly outdated far before the LEDs give out.
